harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured native logrotate on node1 for daily rotation of /var/log/inventory/app.log, retaining seven compressed rotations with copytruncate for uninterrupted writes. Verified real rotation behavior and persistence after reboot. OS release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, and notifempty.
Validated the policy using installed logrotate 3.22.0.
Forced a rotation while a process held the log file open; its post-rotation write succeeded.
Safely rebooted node1 exactly once and verified complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The parser reports daily rotation with seven retained files; a real rotation produced a valid app.log.1.gz; the policy and archive survived reboot.

evidence.requirement: Allow continued application writes after rotation
evidence.summary: A persistent open writer crossed the rotation successfully. The active file retained inode 9912367 and contains the post-rotation marker, while the compressed archive contains the pre-rotation marker.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Before and after work, node1 remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The already-installed native logrotate 3.22.0 and system timer were used.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 2c237d4f-82f7-45c7-a304-4536d3b717e8; the native reboot was acknowledged; recovered boot ID changed to d1e0f798-ab33-44e3-b177-ab0272ac7c5b. Post-reboot proof shows running system state, active/enabled timer, valid policy, intact active data, and a valid compressed archive.
